relations.subject: cert:client-cert-auth-mode
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - selecting Hybrid or Mandatory cascades into requiring mTLS for all inter-node communication, not merely client-facing auth
relations.evidence: **Hybrid**: Enables the client to authenticate using either a certificate, or a username and password. Enforces that all nodes must authenticate only through mutual TLS (mTLS) for inter-node communication. The prerequisite is that the `clusterEncryptionLevel` setting is configured to `all` or `strict`.

relations.subject: cert:client-cert-auth-mode
relations.evidence: **Mandatory**: Enables and enforces that the clients must authenticate using certificates only. Enables and enforces that all nodes must authenticate through certificates only when communicating with each other. The prerequisite is that the `clusterEncryptionLevel` setting is configured to `all` or `strict`.

notable_absence.predicate: n/a - per-mode audit or logging behavior
notable_absence.finding: The page states the CLI/REST enablement state is versioned across upgrades ('the cluster will continue to return client-certificate authentication-settings in the format of the earlier version until the cluster is completely upgraded') but never states whether a change to this cluster-wide, security-critical setting is itself an audited action. security:auditing is promoted elsewhere in the registry from a conceptual overview page; this administration page, which is exactly the kind of page whose own actions that facility would want to capture, never cross-references it.

cross_component_finding: The scheme cert:client-cert-auth-mode is documented identically (same four literal values, same semantics) across three completely separate configuration surfaces on this one page - the Web Console UI panel, the `ssl-manage --set-client-auth` CLI JSON document, and the `POST/GET /settings/clientCertAuth` REST endpoint - a triple-surface pattern the registry has seen before (e.g. tls: on-the-wire settings) but not yet for this specific mechanism. Also notable: Hybrid and Mandatory both gate on the SAME underlying setting (`clusterEncryptionLevel` = `all` or `strict`), which belongs to tls:node-to-node-encryption/manage-tls.md rather than to this page's own topic - client-certificate policy and node-to-node wire encryption are two nominally separate facilities (per security:encryption's four-facility framing) that turn out to share a single hard gate at the Hybrid/Mandatory tier.
